alt.en: A cropped book page of small printed type: family entries numbered 10 to 16, the last reading "Abraham, b. Oct. 13, 1807; joined the family of Shakers, at Enfield, in 1827".
alt.es: Recorte de una página de libro con letra impresa pequeña: entradas de una familia numeradas del 10 al 16; la última dice "Abraham, b. Oct. 13, 1807; joined the family of Shakers, at Enfield, in 1827".

caption.en: The entry for Abraham Perkins, born 13 October 1807, in M. T. Runnels's History of Sanbornton, New Hampshire (1881): it says he joined the Shakers at Enfield in 1827 and became "a preacher and temporal adviser" there and at Canterbury.
caption.es: La entrada de Abraham Perkins, nacido el 13 de octubre de 1807, en la History of Sanbornton, New Hampshire de M. T. Runnels (1881): dice que se unió a los shakers de Enfield en 1827 y llegó a ser "a preacher and temporal adviser" (predicador y consejero en lo temporal) allí y en Canterbury.

source: M. T. Runnels, History of Sanbornton, New Hampshire, vol. 2, Genealogies (Boston: Alfred Mudge & Son, 1881), p. 550, the Perkins family, Nos. 10 to 16 (detail)
library: University of New Hampshire Library (scan on the Internet Archive)
licenceEvidence: Printed 1881 (title page: 'Boston, Mass.: Alfred Mudge & Son, Printers ... 1881'); author Moses Thurston Runnels died 1902 (Internet Archive record: 'Runnels, M. T. (Moses Thurston), 1830-1902'; 'possible-copyright-status: NOT_IN_COPYRIGHT')
credit: University of New Hampshire Library, via the Internet Archive

alt.en: Black-and-white photograph of a tall granite building with a steep gable end, rows of plain windows and a small open cupola topped by a cross, standing on a lawn with paths.
alt.es: Fotografía en blanco y negro de un edificio alto de granito con un hastial empinado, filas de ventanas sencillas y una pequeña cúpula abierta rematada por una cruz, sobre un césped con senderos.

caption.en: The Great Stone Dwelling of the Shakers' Church Family at Enfield, New Hampshire, built from 1837 to 1841 to house the whole family and photographed in 1978: Abraham Perkins, the medium named under this song, became an associate elder of that family in 1845.
caption.es: La Great Stone Dwelling (gran casa de piedra) de la Church Family de los shakers en Enfield, Nuevo Hampshire, construida entre 1837 y 1841 para alojar a toda la familia y fotografiada en 1978: Abraham Perkins, el médium nombrado al pie de esta canción, pasó a ser anciano asociado de esa familia en 1845.

source: Historic American Buildings Survey, Jack Boucher, photographer, June 1978, WEST AND SOUTH ELEVATIONS - Shaker Church Family Dwelling House, State Route 4A, Enfield, Grafton County, NH (HABS NH-75)
library: Library of Congress, Prints & Photographs Division
licenceEvidence: Library of Congress rights advisory: 'No known restrictions on images made by the U.S. Government; images copied from other sources may be restricted.' (https://www.loc.gov/rr/print/res/114_habs.html); the HABS index to photographs for NH-75 names 'Jack Boucher, Photographer June 1978' for this view

alt.en: A cropped page of printed verse, numbered 4, beginning "The pleasures of earth are but transient and vain" and including the line "While heavenly treasures the faithful do gain".
alt.es: Recorte de una página con versos impresos, numerados con un 4, que empiezan "The pleasures of earth are but transient and vain" e incluyen el verso "While heavenly treasures the faithful do gain".

caption.en: Not this song but another Shaker hymn of the same year: verse 4 of "Choice of Pleasures", from Watervliet, New York, in A Collection of Millennial Hymns, printed by the Shakers at Canterbury, New Hampshire, in 1847. It too promises the faithful treasure: "heavenly treasures the faithful do gain".
caption.es: No es esta canción, sino otro himno shaker del mismo año: la cuarta estrofa de "Choice of Pleasures" (la elección de los placeres), de Watervliet, Nueva York, en A Collection of Millennial Hymns, impreso por los shakers en Canterbury, Nuevo Hampshire, en 1847. También promete tesoros a los fieles: "heavenly treasures the faithful do gain" (tesoros celestiales que ganan los fieles).

source: A Collection of Millennial Hymns, Adapted to the Present Order of the Church (Canterbury, N.H.: Printed in the United Society, 1847), p. 100, hymn 73, "Choice of Pleasures", verse 4 (the hymn is signed "Watervliet, N. Y." on p. 101)
library: Princeton Theological Seminary Library (scan on the Internet Archive)
licenceEvidence: Printed 1847 (title page: 'Printed in the United Society, Canterbury, N. H. 1847'); no author named, the hymn signed only 'Watervliet, N. Y.'; an anonymous work published 178 years ago
credit: Princeton Theological Seminary Library, via the Internet Archive
